samples.summary: Gate 1's header now specifies a rule the code does not implement: it says "EVERY run of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ... concluded `success`", but `ciConclusion()` implements newest-run-wins (and `checks.mjs`/`harness-engineering.md`/the lessons file all explain that the every-run rule was deliberately reverted). The file header is the spec a reader of the gate consults first, so this leaves the module's own contract contradicting the design doc and the implementation.
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:7 "1. EVERY run of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the PR head SHA concluded `success`" vs checks.mjs:69 "THE NEWEST RUN WINS" and docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1915 "**The newest CI run wins...**"

samples.summary: The change adopts a repo-wide rule — a `workflow_run` trigger's `workflows:` filter matches only a display name, so consumers must assert `github.event.workflow_run.path` — and applies it to every CI consumer, but `capture-collect.yml` consumes `workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]` with no path clause and no mention in the design doc's enumeration of which workflows need one and why. Impact is limited (its `permissions:` are read-only; it writes via a scoped token to another repo), but the newly documented rule is now applied inconsistently and the doc's enumeration reads as exhaustive.
samples.evidence: capture-collect.yml:67-69 triggers on display names only; harness-engineering.md's new "The trigger side needs the same guard" paragraph lists only agent-review-panel / agent-iterate-ci / ci-report and excuses docker-publish / publish-ghpage, never mentioning capture-collect.
searchedFor: grep 'path' in harness-engineering.md's new trigger paragraph

samples.summary: The `ciConclusion` docstring points readers at a test called `ciTriggersKeepOneRunPerHeadSha` in `checks.test.mjs`; the test added by this diff is actually titled "ci.yml's triggers keep exactly one CI run per PR head SHA". A grep for the named identifier finds nothing, which is exactly the kind of pointer this file's commenting style relies on.
samples.evidence: checks.mjs:73 vs checks.test.mjs test("ci.yml's triggers keep exactly one CI run per PR head SHA", ...)

samples.summary: `const CI_PATH = CI_WORKFLOW_PATH;` adds a second local name for the shared constant in the same file that just imported it; the alias buys nothing and gives future readers two spellings of the same value.
samples.evidence: import { CI_WORKFLOW_PATH, ... } from "./checks.mjs"; const CI_PATH = CI_WORKFLOW_PATH;
